correctness.rationale: The frozen FKM recursion enumerates binary necklaces once; its terminal period p is the size of the labeled rotation orbit. For p<n the word and all its rotations are proper powers and hence bordered. For p=n the count of unbordered starting positions is constant on the orbit, so adding n to its bin is correct. Testing borders only through floor(n/2) loses none: a longer border gives period d=n−b<n/2, and using the largest positive multiple of d less than n gives a border of length at most d. An independently written direct exhaustive computation visited every labeled binary word at every length 1–28, without orbit weights. For each border length b it located runs of b consecutive cyclic equalities between bits at distance b, marking the corresponding rotation starts at the shifted positions. Counting unmarked starts reproduced all 29 CSV columns in each of the 28 rows, including every cell at lengths 26–28. At n=28 the first and second raw sums are 2,012,861,088 and 15,596,094,136; division by 2^28 and subtraction of the squared mean yield the stated exact mean and variance. The highest nonzero index is 13 with 5,040 words. Row totals, zero bins and first moments agreed with independent identities. At n=1 both words are unbordered; for n≥2, a nonprimitive word has none and the lexicographically least and greatest rotations of a primitive word are distinct unbordered words, consistent with the missing j=1 bin.
residual_risks: The replay is exact only at lengths 1–28. It neither proves an arbitrary-length formula for the frequencies or variance nor asserts any larger cutoff.

evidence: Clokie et al. pp. 2–3 discuss the maximum classification, and p. 12 Theorem 14 gives n u_2(n)/2^n for the expectation. Indeed 28 is not of the exceptional lengths permitting 14, and the known even-length maximum is 13. Holub–Müller pp. 1, 4 and 7 study words with exactly two unbordered conjugates.

value.rationale: The statistic is motivated by the established extremal and mean problems for unbordered conjugates: they leave open how typical or rare any number of unbordered starts is. The table measures this variation across all labeled binary words at 28 consecutive lengths. At n=28 alone it distinguishes a central bin of 73,564,148 words at j=8 from just 5,040 of 2^28 words at the known maximum. A researcher studying dependence between rotations, exact moments or near-extremal populations can use these actual frequencies; neither the first moment nor a low-weight slice supplies them. The bounded cutoff is a reproducible complete census, not a substitute for an asymptotic distribution theorem.
residual_risks: No unrestricted-length variance formula, asymptotic behavior, or cutoff beyond length 28 is established.
